documents.title: Admission History and Physical
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
ADMISSION H&P -- regional hospital, Internal Medicine
Admitted 05/31/2026

CC: right flank pain, painful urination, fever.

HPI: 37-year-old woman with Von Hippel-Lindau syndrome, prior clear cell RCC (left radical nephrectomy, solitary right kidney) and type 2 diabetes on metformin, presenting with two days of constant right flank pain radiating toward the groin and burning with urination. Fever and chills since yesterday. Denies nausea, vomiting or diarrhea.

PMH: T2DM (well controlled on metformin), HTN, VHL (cerebellar and spinal hemangioblastomas, retinal angiomas, right renal lesion under surveillance), Cushing syndrome, PCOS, hyperinsulinemia, bipolar I.
PSH: left radical nephrectomy for clear cell RCC (age 31).
Home meds: olanzapine 10 mg qhs, lisinopril 10 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, ketoconazole 200 mg tid, metformin.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father VHL; mother T2DM, HTN; maternal uncle bipolar.
SH: never smoker; 1-2 drinks monthly; part-time administrative assistant.

Exam: T 38.5 C (101.3 F), BP 130/85, HR 88. Alert and oriented. Right costovertebral angle tenderness. Abdomen soft, no guarding. Heart regular, lungs clear.

Labs: WBC 12.0, Hgb 13.2, BUN 18, creatinine 1.0. UA with pyuria and bacteriuria. Urine and blood cultures sent.

Assessment: Acute right pyelonephritis in a solitary kidney.
Plan: ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily, IV fluids, acetaminophen for fever, renal ultrasound to exclude obstruction. Continue home medications.

Hospital Medicine

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit 05/31/2026 -- Discharge 06/02/2026

Diagnosis: Acute right pyelonephritis, solitary kidney.

Course: Treated with ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily. Renal ultrasound: no hydronephrosis, stone or abscess; known right renal lesion and cysts unchanged. Defervesced by hospital day 2, flank pain improving, eating well. Urine culture: E. coli >100,000 CFU/mL, susceptible to ceftriaxone, ciprofloxacin and TMP-SMX, resistant to ampicillin. Blood cultures no growth to date.

Discharge medications:
- NEW ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO twice daily x 5 days (7 days total therapy)
- continue metformin 1000 mg BID, olanzapine 10 mg qhs, lisinopril 10 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, ketoconazole 200 mg tid
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: PCP within one week. Return for recurrent fever, vomiting, or worsening pain.

Hospital Medicine
